{{Quote|Justice by any means. The bounty hunter guild. It's what you pay for.|translated=1|A [[Huttese]] advert for the Guild played on board the ''[[Morenia]]''|audio=BHGAd-WildCard.flac|<ref name="WildCard">''[[Star Wars Outlaws]]''</ref>}}
The '''Bounty Hunters' Guild''' ('''BHG'''), also known as the '''Bondsman Guild''' or simply the '''Bounty Guild''', was an institution that regulated the complicated profession that was the [[Bounty hunter|bounty hunting]] trade throughout [[the galaxy]]. Ensuring the legality of hunting for its members, it worked alongside [[Galaxy|galactic]] governments and curated [[Bounty|bounties]] for its members. From the [[Republic Era]] to the [[New Republic Era]], the Guild operated with members of various [[species]] and [[droid]] models, both with loyal and independent programming, and had a [[Bounty Hunter Code|Code]] that hunters were mandated to stand by. During the [[Galactic Civil War]] and into the [[time]] of the [[New Republic]], the Bounty Hunters' Guild had close ties to the [[Galactic Empire]] and its remnants, although there was a chance it would favor the [[Resistance]] during the [[Cold War]] due to the [[First Order]]'s reluctance to deal business with its hunters.

==Description==
===Legality===
{{Quote|By the authority of the Bounty Hunters' Guild, you are now my acquisition.|Bossk|<ref name="Destiny">{{Destiny|set=Spark of Hope|cardname=Bounty Hunters' Guild|link=https://swdestinydb.com/card/11046}}</ref>}}
During the [[time]] of the [[Galactic Republic]] and its successor, the [[Galactic Empire]], proper certification was required in the [[bounty]] hunting profession to ensure the legality of the processes involved, specifically the handling of wanted quarry and the delivery of a posted bounty by the issuing authority. Working alongside galactic governments, the [[Bounty hunter|Bounty Hunters]]' Guild<ref name="TSWB" />—abbreviated to "BHG"<ref name="Rebel Files">''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]''</ref> and also known as the Bondsman Guild<ref name="Chapter 1" />—expedited much of the bureaucratic hassle required to obtain the necessary legal permits for Guild members, allowing them to hunt across [[the galaxy]] with an official license.<ref name="TSWB" /> Indeed, governments like the Empire made active use of bounty hunters to fulfill their needs. As such, those same hunters were expected to not take on contracts that interfered with Imperial operations, lest they become a fugitive of Imperial law themselves.<ref name="BWR1">[[Boba Fett — Black, White & Red 1|''Boba Fett — Black, White & Red'' 1]]</ref>

In the [[Imperial Era]], the [[Imperial Office of Criminal Investigations]] had an entire branch dedicated to working with the guild, and wealthy [[Moff]]s were willing to pay hunters to handle their issues.<ref name="Rebel Files" /> Procedures on how hunters were to operate and how others were to interact with them were laid out in the [[Bondsman Guild Protocol]].<ref name="Chapter 1" /> Under Guild authority, a bounty hunter had the right to take a target captive.<ref name="Destiny" /> Subparagraph 16 of the bondsman protocol outlined the authority a hunter had to immediately receive the bounty they were in pursuit of.<ref name="Chapter 1" />

===Guild hubs===
[[File:GuildHubCarajam-AORBobaFett1.jpg|thumb|left|300px|A guild hub on Carajam]]
The Bounty Hunters' Guild maintained hubs on worlds such as [[Carajam]]<ref name="AoR-Boba" /> and [[Nevarro]]<ref name="Nevarro DB" /> that functioned as [[cantina]]s. Installed with a [[droid detector]] at its entrance, the cantina on Carajam was populated with a multitude of [[species]], including [[Cerean]], [[Ithorian]], [[Kel Dor]], [[Morseerian]], [[Neimoidian]], [[Rodian]], [[Togruta]], and [[Trandoshan]] patrons. A [[Unidentified Bounty Hunters' Guild agent|Rutian Twi'lek]] served as an agent of the Guild, liaising with hunters on Guild bounties at the cantina's central bar.<ref name="AoR-Boba" /> The Empire preferred to pay hunters by transfer register instead of hard [[currency]],<ref name="EG">''[[Ezra's Gamble]]''</ref> and after a successful hunt, Guild members could be payed directly to their account by the Guild agent, although the [[Twi'lek]] offered to deduct from [[Boba Fett]]'s payout for a special deal on the [[Jorgan Spa]], which she thought the hunter deserved. Bounties at Guild hubs were identified through holograms beside the bar. Larger bounties were advertised on poster; such was the case for the quarry [[Zingo Gabnit]], on whom the [[Rutian]] agent provided additional information to Fett.<ref name="AoR-Boba" />

On Imperial worlds, [[Posting agency|posting agencies]] were established as offices for bounty hunters. Posting offices were installed with computer consoles that permitted hunters to accept Galactic Empire–issued bounties, and individuals were employed at booths in posting agencies to oversee the offices, as well as to restrict research on the [[Imperial Enforcement DataCore]] to ranking Imperial officers and licensed bounty hunters.<ref name="EG" />

Described by bounty hunter [[Din Djarin]] as a "hive" for people of his profession,<ref name="Chapter 8">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 8: Redemption}}</ref> Nevarro was a hub for the Guild in the early [[Standard day|days]] of the [[New Republic]]<ref name="Nevarro DB">{{Databank|nevarro|Nevarro}}</ref> and home to its own Guild branch, known simply as the [[Nevarro Hunters]].<ref name="Chapter 21" /> Pirate<ref name="Chapter 17">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 17: The Apostate}}</ref> and guild operations were managed from the [[Nevarro school|Nevarro Common House]], a cantina in [[Nevarro City]].<ref name="The Mandalorian Handbook">''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian Handbook]]''</ref> Ultimately, however, such criminal activity would be forced off Nevarro after it fell under the control of [[Greef Karga]],<ref name="Chapter 17">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 17: The Apostate}}</ref> former [[Guild Master]] of the Nevarro Hunters who decided to bring the world down a new path.<ref name="Chapter 21" />

===Membership===
====Bounty hunters====
{{Quote|This is my first job. You can keep the money, all of it. I just need this job to get into the Guild.|Toro Calican, to Din Djarin|<ref name="Chapter 5" />}}
[[File:GuildedBountyHunter-AaA.png|thumb|right|160px|A guilded bounty hunter]]
The Bounty Hunters' Guild's membership was composed of bounty hunters of various species as well as independent [[droid]] models.<ref name="AoR-Boba" /> In order to get into the Bounty Hunters' Guild, a hopeful bounty hunter needed to complete a bounty hunt.<ref name="Chapter 5" /> Non-Guild hunters did exist out in the [[galaxy]] and worked at cheaper rates, although Guild Master Greef Karga regarded such individuals as being more messy than those certified by the Guild. Some bounties called for the execution of a target.<ref name="Chapter 1" /> All the same, freelance [[assassin]]s had a league of their own known as the [[Assassin's Guild]].<ref name="Vader 18">[[Darth Vader (2020) 18|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 18]]</ref> The Nevarro Hunters maintained favorable relations with pirate groups, including [[Gorian Shard's pirate crew|Gorian Shard's gang]].<ref name="Chapter 17" />

Bounty hunting droids made ideal business partners for their internal toolsets, which could apply healing [[bacta]] sprays to organics or lift heavy objects. Bounty droids were also physically tougher than most organics, and approached their trade with machinelike efficiency, providing a potentially lifesaving alternative to living hunters when tracking down high-risk suspects. However, like many other droids, bounty hunting droids struggled with ambiguity and had a slavish regard for the rules, making them potentially ill-suited for the more complicated intricacies of the profession. Additionally, their programming forbid them from being captured, and bounty droids would engage their self-destruct protocols when if they thought apprehension was imminent.<ref name="TSWB" />

[[File:BountyHunters1-Movie-textless.png|thumb|left|250px|The droid IG-88 and human Boba Fett were both Guild members]]
Droids from the [[IG-series|IG family]] either served as private security or freelance members of the Guild,<ref name="TSWB" /> earning them a reputation as usually being bounty hunters.<ref name="Chapter 8" /> [[IG-11]] was a fully-fledged member of the Guild. Although following a strict programming as a bounty droid,<ref name="TSWB" /> IG-11 specialized in terminating whatever he was assigned to by the Guild and thus was often ordered to kill his targets, instead of being tasked with bounties that needed to be brought in alive.<ref name="Greef Transmission">{{AtomicMassGames|url=transmission/greef-karga-ig-11-assassin-droid|text=Greef Karga & IG-11, Assassin Droid}}</ref> One of a set of five identical [[IG-88 assassin droid]]s<ref name="CVD">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]''</ref> manufactured by [[Holowan Laboratories]]<ref name="USW">''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]''</ref> who [[Holowan Laboratories massacre|slaughtered their constructors and escaped their laboratories]] into the wider galaxy,<ref name="CVD" /> unit [[IG-88B]],<ref name="IG-88B">{{ForceCollection|IG-88B|star=2}}</ref> or IG-88 for short, had independent programming<ref name="Sideshow">{{SideshowCite|set=Sideshow Collectibles|text=Sixth Scale Figures|pack=IG-88|link=collectibles/star-wars-ig-88-sideshow-collectibles-1000292}}</ref> and was a member of the Guild.<ref name="Build R2 16">{{BuildR2Cite|16|Droid Directory}}</ref> He was feared in his bounty hunting career<ref name="Sideshow" /> as one of the top five hunters of his era.<ref name="Star Wars: Droidography">''[[Star Wars: Droidography]]''</ref>

Whereas IG-11 demonstrated concern for the rewards his hunts would generate,<ref name="Chapter 1" /> IG-88 did work in the bounty hunting trade as a way to murder more organics.<ref name="IG-88 Image">[[:File:WBHIG88Frenz.jpg]]</ref> Still, IG-88 also showed concern for earning credits from his work, even showing willingness to take in his prey alive.<ref name="Triplecross">{{FOD|Triplecross}}</ref>  Although IG-88's work distracted from his fellow assassin droid [[IG-88A]] and that unit's [[IG-88A's plan to overthrow organic life|plan to overthrow organic life]],<ref name="HC 2">{{HelmetCollectionCite|2|Weapons & Uniforms}}</ref> IG-88 was even willing to hunt his fellow droids for a bounty placed on them.<ref name="D-Squad 2">[[Dark Droids: D-Squad 2|''Dark Droids: D-Squad'' 2]]</ref>

====Bondsmen and leadership====
In addition to recruiting hunters, the Guild employed the services of<ref name="BH3">[[Bounty Hunters 3|''Bounty Hunters'' 3]]</ref> Guild Masters<ref name="Chapter 21" /> and [[Bail bondsman|bail bondsmen]].<ref name="Sisters">{{StoryCite|story=Sisters|book=Age of Republic Special 1}}</ref> Although some hunters were people who preferred working alone,<ref name="Greef Transmission" /> bondsmen were individuals who brokered bounties with hunters.<ref name="Chapter 1" /><ref name="Sisters" /> Serving as the intermediary between the hunters and the client, a bondsman offered jobs and paid out upon a successful hunt,<ref name="Sisters" /> with Guild Master<ref name="Chapter 21" /> Greef Karga doing the same for the guild branch based on Nevarro.<ref name="Chapter 1" /> In [[9 ABY]], five [[Standard year|years]] after the fragmentation of the Empire at the [[Battle of Endor]],<ref name="Date">{{MandoDate|1}}</ref> Karga operated as a Guild Master<ref name="Chapter 21" /> and Guild expeditor on Nevarro, acting as a middle-man between clients and hunters.<ref name="Karga-DB" /> Karga received a cut of the bounty from the former Imperial known as "[[the Client]]" when bounty hunter Din Djarin completed a mission for the man.<ref name="Chapter 3">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 3: The Sin}}</ref>

[[File:KargaGekkoFaceMando-TMCh3.png|thumb|right|300px|Greef Karga leads Guild hunters against Din Djarin.]]
All the same, it would be incorrect to say there were "pencil-pushers" amongst the Guild's ranks; Karga himself, for example, was willing to personally take on [[mercenary]] work.<ref name="Greef Transmission" /> When Djarin then broke the Bounty Hunter Code, Karga personally led the Nevarro Hunters into battle against the rogue agent.<ref name="Chapter 3" /> He also engineered a plot to assassinate Djarin but ultimately changed his mind by gunning down his own associates.<ref name="Chapter 7">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 7: The Reckoning}}</ref> Indeed, the Guild survived over its lifetime because of its pragmatism: high-ranking jobs in the Guild could call for a degree of redundancy and see turn over whenever a post suddenly became vacant<ref name="Greef Transmission" /> as, just like any other member of the Guild, a Guild Master could end up dead.<ref name="Chapter 3" />

Leadership within the guild was subject to elections. In the lead-up to guild elections, high-level communications containing [[Hologram|holographic]] advertisements were sent out by various candidates to other guild members. Guild hunter [[Bossk'wassak'Cradossk|Bossk]] ignored such communications as they swamped his inbox, and removed them as they appeared. Bossk's own father, [[Cradossk]],<ref name="ToothClaw">{{StoryCite|story=Tooth and Claw|book=From a Certain Point of View: The Empire Strikes Back}}</ref> was a major member of the Guild.<ref name="Rebel Files" />

===Acquisitions===
{{Quote|I am Lieutenant Masil Veit, communications officer on the Star Destroyer ''Executor'', and am contacting you based on the recommendation of your guild. My commander will pay a significant bounty for the capture of a Corellian freighter called the ''Millennium Falcon''.|A message addressed by Imperial officer [[Masil Veit]] to the guild hunter Bossk|<ref name="ToothClaw" />}}
[[File:BobaBlasterpoint-AORBobaFett1.jpg|thumb|left|260px|Bounties posted through the Guild offered lucrative work for hunters]]
The Guild regulated bounties that included criminals, thieves, murderers, and even bounty hunters. Zingo Gabnit, whom the Guild offered 100,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]] for, was a bounty hunter who was listed by the Empire as a rebel collaborator, and, most importantly to the Guild, violated the [[Bounty Hunter Code]].<ref name="AoR-Boba" />

The Galactic Empire was a major client of the Guild. For high-level bounties, the Empire contacted guild hunters individually, with their bounty hunter selection based upon Guild recommendation. Bossk was offered a high-level bounty personally posted by Darth Vader, and while he could not locate the designated rendezvous coordinates with Vader's flagship due to technical difficulties, Bossk did not request the guild to help him pinpoint the Imperial address that sent him Vader's offer for fear of relaying his interest to the guild, which risked competition with other guild hunters if they were to be alerted to the bounty.<ref name="ToothClaw" />

===The hunt===
{{Quote|It's not slow at all, actually. Very busy. They just don't want to pay Guild rates. They don't mind if things get sloppy.|Greef Karga, on the bounty hunting field|<ref name="Chapter 1" />}}
The regulatory body of<ref name="EG" /> the complicated<ref name="Chapter 1" /> and risky<ref name="Greef Transmission" /> bounty hunting trade, the guild curated bounties for its members.<ref name="EG" /> Quarries were identified in individual [[holopuck]]s, simple holographic devices that displayed an image of the quarry, their name, and the bounty payout. Used alongside a [[tracking fob]], the information on the puck allowed Guild members to hunt down their quarry to the edge of the galaxy.<ref name="Holopuck">{{Databank|holopuck|holopuck}}</ref> Upon picking up such devices at Guild hubs, Guild hunters accepted the bounty and proceeded to their hunt.<ref name="Chapter 1" />

Members of the Guild were required to follow the Bounty Hunter Code,<ref name="Target Vader 1">[[Target Vader 1|''Target Vader'' 1]]</ref> and, during the reign of the Empire, the guild was given authority by the Imperial Office of Criminal Investigations to issue [[Imperial Peace-Keeping Certificate]]s,<ref name="Ezra's Journal">''[[Rebel Journal by Ezra Bridger]]''</ref> which allowed its holder to operate as a licensed hunter on Imperial worlds and access to the Imperial Enforcement DataCore at posting agencies.<ref name="EG" /> Greef Karga thought highly of Guild work, which be believed prevented bounty hunting from getting "sloppy," as he saw across the non-guild affiliated field.<ref name="Chapter 1" /> Nonetheless, [[Neimoidian Royal Guard]] [[Ruug Quarnom]] described guild hunters as not being "precise" actors in most operations.<ref name="Brotherhood">''[[Brotherhood (novel)|Brotherhood]]''</ref> The higher bar of quality allowed the guild to charge higher for its work compared to independent bounty hunters, which had the effect of more parsimonious individuals refusing to pay those higher rates and instead not minding if the work got "sloppy" if it still got done.<ref name="Chapter 1" />

===The Code and other policies===
{{Main|Bounty Hunter Code}}
{{Quote|Members of the guild are expected to live by a code, which is intended to keep them from poaching another hunter's bounty, killing another guild member in good standing, or taking a personal interest in their targets once the bounty has been paid. In theory, it is a good system to help regulate some very bad people. However, not every bounty hunter belongs to the guild. And even of those who do, not all adhere strictly to the code.|Hondo Ohnaka|<ref name="TSotBH">''[[Star Wars: The Secrets of the Bounty Hunters]]''</ref>}}
[[File:ValanceDefeatsBossk-BountyHunters3.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Beilert Valance violated the Bounty Hunter Code on multiple occasions.]]
Members of the guild were mandated to uphold the Bounty Hunter Code,<ref name="Target Vader 1" /> which forbade members to slay another guild hunter,<ref name="AoR-Boba" /> or steal another hunter's bounty.<ref name="Target Vader 1" /> The Code also forbade hunters from asking about their bounties once delivered, requiring that events that transpired between the time of accepting and delivering the bounty be immediately forgotten.<ref name="Chapter 3" /> Additionally, when the guild assigned one of its members to pursue the subject of a government bounty, only that particular hunter was authorized to go after that particular acquisition.<ref name="EG" /> Although such restrictions were guild policy, Beilert Valance was a guild member who was known for flouting the Code.<ref name="Target Vader 1" /> Around 9 ABY, a galactic recession led to exceptionally low bounties, and as a result, at the request of the client ordering the bounty or at the discretion of the local Guild boss, high-value targets could have been assigned to several bounty hunters.<ref name="100 objects">''[[Star Wars 100 Objects]]''</ref>

For his violations of the Guild code, Valance became a valid target for a Guild member to bring in.<ref name="Target Vader 1" /> While the Guild's bureaucracy held members in check over policies, the [[Unbroken Clan]] criminal syndicate's [[General]] [[Vukorah]] had the ability to circumvent the bureaucracy by means of credits.<ref name="BH6">[[Bounty Hunters 6|''Bounty Hunters'' 6]]</ref> Even by the aftermath of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]]'s decisive victory at the [[Battle of Yavin]], no official policy was published by the guild on accepting rebel jobs. As a result, [[Cynabar's InfoNet]] recommended to independent hunters willing to risk working with the Alliance to deal with third-party bounty brokers only.<ref name="Rebel Files" />

==History==
===Republic Era===
During the [[Nihil conflict]] of the [[High Republic Era]], [[Lourna Dee]], herself a former [[Tempest Runner]] of the [[Nihil]] [[Pirate|marauders]], formed a bounty guild known as the [[Tempest Breakers]] with her former Nihil subordinate [[Quin Carree]].<ref name="Tempest Breaker" /> Bossk, a Trandoshan known for hunting [[Wookiee]]s, was a member of the Bounty Hunters' Guild during the [[Clone Wars]]. Such information was known to the [[Jedi Master]] [[Quinlan Vos]], who specialized in undercover operations.<ref name="DD">''[[Dark Disciple]]''</ref> During the [[Mission to Cato Neimoidia|investigation]] into the [[Cadesura disaster]], [[Neimoidian]] royal guard [[Ruug Quarnom]]—who had experience working with bounty hunters and, thus, understood their standard operating procedure—ruled out the BHG as a culprit, instead discovering that the attack had been far too precise for something like the guild.<ref name="Brotherhood" />

===Imperial Era===
{{Quote|Our agent in the Bounty Hunters Guild reports that sentiment is trending negative toward the Rebellion as the Empire increases its use of guild services. In other words, Cradossk is making a killing.|Cassian Andor's report to Davits Draven, ''The Rebel Files''|<ref name="Rebel Files" />}}
In the early Imperial Era, [[Ciddarin Scaleback]] had several contacts within the Guild, and used them to find information about the bounty hunter [[Fennec Shand]] as part of a deal with [[Clone Force 99]].<ref name="Rampage">{{TBB|Rampage (episode)}}</ref>

[[File:BountyHuntersGuild-SoH.png|thumb|left|270px|Dengar, Boba Fett, and Bossk were all members of the Guild and took jobs for the Empire.]]
In the Imperial Era, the Bounty Hunters' Guild was allowed to issue Imperial Peace-Keeping Certificates to their bounty hunters,<ref name="Ezra's Journal" /> allowing them access to the Imperial Enforcement Datacore. Guild member Bossk took on bounties in Imperial territory, with one hunt involving a partnership with a street orphan named [[Ezra Bridger]] that resulted in the Imperial [[HoloNet News]] reporting of the Guild member's "courageous" actions, publicizing Bossk as a hero of justice.<ref name="EG" />

During the [[Galactic Civil War]], [[Rebel Alliance Intelligence Service|Alliance Intelligence]] agent [[Cassian Jeron Andor|Cassian Andor]] gave an assessment of the Guild to General [[Davits Draven]] in ''[[The Rebel Files]]''. In search of allies, the Rebel Alliance found that, through a rebel agent in the Guild, sentiment was trending negative amongst hunters regarding the Rebel Alliance, and as the Empire made greater use of Guild services against the Rebellion, Andor reported in conclusion that "Cradossk is making a killing," and that the Alliance should seek other factions for support in their fight for freedom.<ref name="Rebel Files" />

After being discharged from Imperial service,<ref name="Target Vader 5">[[Target Vader 5|''Target Vader'' 5]]</ref> Beilert Valance became a bounty hunter and began stealing bounties from members of the Guild, breaking the Bounty Hunter Code. [[Xonr]], a member of the Guild, attempted to confront him along with several other bounty hunters over the stolen bounties. Valance, who had in fact lured them there, proceeded to kill them.<ref name="Target Vader 1" />

In the aftermath of the [[Battle of Hoth]], [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] personally posted a bounty on the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]'', a rebel vessel, attracting the guild hunters Bossk, Dengar, Boba Fett, IG-88, [[4-LOM]], and [[Zuckuss]], all of whom were invited to the Imperial [[Super Star Destroyer]] ''[[Executor]]''{{'s}} [[Bridge (starship)|bridge]]. The leader of Vader's personal [[Death Squadron|starfleet]], [[Admiral]] [[Firmus Piett]], expressed his aversion to the Empire's employment of the guild hunters, declaring them as "scum" to a subordinate whilst on duty aboard the ''Executor''{{'s}} [[Bridge (starship)|bridge]].<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref><ref name="ToothClaw" />

===New Republic Era===
====The Mandalorian and the Child====
=====Hunt for the Child=====
{{Main|Hunt for Grogu}}
{{Quote|You are a Guild member? I thought I was the only one on assignment.''"<br />"''That makes two of us.|IG-11 and the Mandalorian|<ref name="Chapter 1" />}}
Following the Empire's major defeat in [[Battle of Endor]]<ref name="Aftermath">[[Aftermath (novel)|''Aftermath'']]</ref> in [[4 ABY]],<ref name="Galactic Atlas">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''</ref> the Rebel Alliance reformed into the [[New Republic]]. Believing the bounty hunting trade was now under threat thanks to the new government, Dengar wanted to form a proper bounty hunter union. His prediction<ref name="Aftermath" /> began to come true<ref name="LD">''[[Aftermath: Life Debt]]''</ref> in [[5 ABY]]<ref name="Life Debt">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''[[Aftermath: Life Debt]]'' to [[5 ABY]].</ref> in the aftermath of the [[attack on Chandrila]], as the New Republic, trying to make sure its security forces look strong, stopped hiring bounty hunters.<ref name="LD" /> Later that year,<ref name="Galactic Atlas" /> the Empire fell in the [[Battle of Jakku]].<ref name="Empire's End">''[[Aftermath: Empire's End]]''</ref>

[[File:Acme-TakeCover.png|thumb|right|250px|IG-11 and Din Djarin were both Guild hunters involved in the search for an Imperial remnant's asset.]]
Around [[9 ABY]], the ongoing [[galactic recession]] led to exceptionally low bounties, making the dangerous profession less attractive. As a result, at the request of the client ordering the bounty or at the discretion of the local Guild boss, high-value targets might be assigned to several bounty hunters equipped with identical tracking fobs.<ref name="100 objects" /> While bounty hunting remained a popular field in that individuals sought the aid of hunters, many of those interested clients were not eager to pay BHG rates and, thus, turned a blind eye to the less professional outcomes of non-guild work, focusing instead on how much cheaper independent hunters came.<ref name="Chapter 1" /> By 9 ABY,<ref name="Date" /> the guild was no longer operating on [[Tatooine]],<ref name="Chapter 5" /> but one subdivision,<ref name="Chapter 1" /> the Nevarro Hunters,<ref name="Chapter 21" /> held operations on the [[Volcano|volcanic]] world of Nevarro<ref name="Chapter 1" /> during the early New Republic period,<ref name="Nevarro DB" /> including in 9 ABY.<ref name="Date" /> During the Imperial Era, Nevarro had already seen use as a bounty-collection spot,<ref name="Bounty Hunters 42">[[Bounty Hunters 42|''Bounty Hunters'' 42]]</ref> yet the planet had remained locked under Imperial control until the Galactic Civil War's end.<ref name="Chapter 7" /> During the early New Republic Era, it would instead be regarded as a hive for bounty hunters.<ref name="Chapter 8" />

A disgraced [[magistrate]]<ref name="Guide to Season One">[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian: Guide to Season One|''Star Wars: The Mandalorian'': Guide to Season One]]</ref> named Greef Karga ran the operations from the [[Nevarro school|cantina]] in the [[Nevarro City|city]]<ref name="Chapter 1" /> as a Guild Master.<ref name="Chapter 21" /> The cantina was built with the cut of treasure Karga recieved from [[Pirate King]] [[Gorian Shard]]. Indeed, Nevarro maintained relations with pirates, with Karga paying members of [[Gorian Shard's pirate crew|Shard's pirate gang]] within the cantina<ref name="Chapter 17">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 17: The Apostate}}</ref> just as he did the bounty hunters;<ref name="Chapter 1" /> according to the pirate [[Vane]], the pirates carried out "murder and mayhem" for that payment.<ref name="Chapter 17" /> In 9 ABY,<ref name="Date" /> all of the bounty hunters operating from Nevarro were [[Hunt for Grogu|hired]] by a member of an [[Gideon's Imperial remnant|Imperial remnant]] known as "the Client" to capture or kill a target known as "[[Din Grogu|the asset]]." The asset was being held by a [[Unidentified Nikto mercenary gang|company]] of [[Nikto]] [[Mercenary|mercenaries]] at their [[Nikto hideout|encampment]] on [[Arvala-7]]. Two Guild members, the droid IG-11 and a [[Mandalorian]] Din Djarin, arrived at the encampment and killed the mercenaries. The pair discovered that the asset was an infant of the same [[Yoda's species|species]] as the [[Jedi]] [[Grand Master]] [[Yoda]]. Although the Mandalorian wanted to extract the Child alive, IG-11 intended to kill it, so Djarin shot him in the head to protect the Child.<ref name="Chapter 1" />

Taking the Child back to his [[Razor Crest|ship]], the Mandalorian was attacked by [[Trandoshan bounty hunter gang|three]] Trandoshan bounty hunters, who were also from the Guild to kill the Child. Djarin defeated the bounty hunters, and after having to repair his ship,<ref name="Chapter 2">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 2: The Child}}</ref> returned to Nevarro to hand the Child over the Client. The rest of the Guild despised the Mandalorian for bringing the Child back first, though Karga praised him as his best bounty hunter.<ref name="Chapter 3" />

[[File:HoldTheLine-TMCh3.png|thumb|left|300px|Members of the Guild cut off the Mandalorian's escape after he stole back the Child.]]
However, having become attached to the Child, Djarin returned to the Client's [[Imperial Remnant safe house|facility]] and stole the infant back. After finding their [[tracking fob]]s were activating again, the members of the Guild on Nevarro confronted the Mandalorian, spearheaded by Karga. Djarin fought them, killing several before he was pinned down. His Mandalorian [[The Tribe|allies]] then arrived and began gunning down the other other bounty hunters. Karga attempted to seize the Child at the Mandalorian's ship but was shot by the Mandalorian, who escaped the planet. Thanks to a piece of beskar hidden in his jacket, Karga survived the shot.<ref name="Chapter 3" />

=====Imperial takeover=====
{{Quote|Nevarro is a very fine planet. And now that the scum and villainy have been washed away, it's very respectable again.''"<br />"''As a bounty hunter hive?''"<br />"''Some of my favorite people are bounty hunters.|Karga and the Mandalorian after defeating the Imperial forces on Nevarro|<ref name="Chapter 8" />}}
[[File:Riot_Mar_Ship.png|thumb|right|300px|Riot Mar pursued the Mandalorian in his ship.]]
With Djarin on the run with the Child, the Client took over Guild operations on Nevarro, occupying the city.<ref name="Chapter 7" /> Bounty hunters were sent out to track the pair. A [[Kubaz]] [[Unidentified Kubaz bounty hunter|bounty hunter]] was able to find them on the planet [[Sorgan]], but was shot by the former rebel [[shock trooper]] [[Carasynthia Dune|Cara Dune]].<ref name="Chapter 4">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 4: Sanctuary}}</ref> The bounty hunter [[Riot Mar]] also found the Mandalorian and chased him in his [[Helix J-104 starfighter|Bounty Hunter Fighter]]. Djarin, though, maneuvered behind Mar and destroyed his ship with him inside.<ref name="Chapter 5" />

With Djarin having evaded the Guild's bounty hunters so far, Karga contacted him, pretending to want to betray the Client. In reality, he planned to kill the bounty hunter and take the Child for the Client. Bringing three loyal Guild members with him, Karga met with the Mandalorian in the [[Lava fields]] on Nevarro. Djarin brought his own backup, Dune and the [[Ugnaught]] [[Kuiil]], and so the two parties began traveling for the city and set up camp for the night. That night, they were attacked by a number of [[Nevarro reptavian|native reptavians]], which took away one of Karga's bounty hunters. Karga was poisoned by one of them, but was saved when the Child used [[Force healing]] on him.<ref name="Chapter 7" />

Because of the former night, Karga had a change of mind. The next day his final two bounty hunters made their move to kill the Mandalorian while they looked towards the city on Nevarro. Karga swiftly killed both of them, and revealed to Djarin that his original plan to kill him. The Mandalorian then decided to do the plan Karga initially intended to do which included killing the Client. Karga brought Dune and a cuffed Djarin to the city's cantina and to the Client. However, before they could kill him, the Client's superior, Moff [[Gideon]], had [[Gideon's guard|his death troopers]] kill them before confronting Karga and the others with a [[Gideon's battalion|battalion]].<ref name="Chapter 7" />

Though Karga and his allies engaged the stormtroopers after being reinforced by IG-11,<ref name="Chapter 8" /> who had been reprogrammed by Kuill and, because the Ugnaught had been killed by Imperial [[scout trooper]]s,<ref name="Chapter 7" /> was carrying the Child with him, they were forced to retreat back into the cantina. Escaping into the [[Nevarro sewer]]s to get to the [[Nevarro Mandalorian covert|Mandalorian covert]], they instead found that the Mandalorians had been [[Attack on the Tribe|massacred]], so Djarin confronted Karga, demanding to know if the guild was behind the genocide. Karga told him that was not the case, telling him that the bounty hunters had retreated from Nevarro after the Child's rescue, and [[the Armorer]] soon arrived. She confirmed that Karga was telling the truth and revealed that the Imperials were behind the massacre.<ref name="Chapter 8" />

[[File:ChangeOfPlan-TMCh7.png|thumb|left|330px|Karga betrayed his hunters to save the Mandalorian.]]
As they were meeting with the Armorer, who gave Djarin the task of finding the Child's species and a [[jetpack]], IG-11 took out an advance Imperial team that had entered the sewers. With the exception of the Armorer, they then left to escape to the [[lava fields]] on a [[boat]], but Djarin spotted a [[platoon]]'s worth of [[stormtrooper]]s at their exit. Following<ref name="Chapter 8" /> his new [[nanny droid]]<ref name="TSWB" /> programming to protect the Child and not allow himself to be captured,<ref name="Chapter 8" /> the former bounty droid<ref name="TSWB" /> self-destructed to take out the Imperial [[troop]]s.<ref name="Chapter 8" />

Afterward, Gideon arrived in his [[Outland TIE fighter]], but Djarin used the jetpack to reach the starfighter before taking it down with a [[bomb]]. Djarin then met with his comrades, with Karga, impressed by the hunter's actions, saying his bounty rates had now increased. Dune, who intended to stay on Nevarro, and Karga both felt that the planet had been cleared of its Imperial occupiers. As such, Karga believed that the guild could return the planet, which he felt would make it respectable once again. Though Djarin felt differently, stating that the world would again become a bounty hunter hive, Karga responded by saying that some of his favorite people were hunters. He offered Dune a place in the guild as his enforcer and gave Djarin the chance to rejoin, telling the Mandalorian that he would now have access to any job he wanted. Djarin instead declined, instead leaving to find the Child's species as the Armorer had instructed.<ref name="Chapter 8" />

====Guild losses====
{{Quote|I bounty-hunt for a private client now. No more low-rent Guild jobs.|Pokkit, to Jod Na Nawood|<ref name="SC5">{{SkeletonCrew|You Have a Lot to Learn About Pirates}}</ref>}}
[[File:Pokkit-SWCT.png|thumb|right|250px|The bounty hunter Pokkit (pictured) left the Bounty Hunter's Guild on the belief that it only afford low-rent work.]]
As Djarin and Grogu left the planet, Karga and Dune were walking back to Nevarro city. Unknown to them all, Gideon had survived the crash of his TIE<ref name="Chapter 8" /> and his remnant continued operations in an [[Nevarro Imperial base|Imperial base]] located away from the city. Rather than let it become a home to the Guild once more, Karga and Dune, who became the city's [[marshal]], focused on cleaning up the planet to make it respectable. In fact, the cantina<ref name="Siege">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 12: The Siege}}</ref> where bounty hunters<ref name="Chapter 3" /> and pirates had once met was transformed into a school.<ref name="Chapter 17" /> During Grogu and Djarin's return to the planet, the Mandalorian bounty hunter worked with Dune, Karga, and the Fledgling Mythrol<ref name="Siege" /> he had once captured for Karga<ref name="Chapter 1" /> in order to destroy [[Nevarro Imperial base|Gideon's last stronghold on Nevarro]].<ref name="Siege" /> While Dune would depart to work for the New Republic, Karga continued to push for reform on Nevarro, turning it into what he considered a "respectable" planet<ref name="Chapter 17" /> and ensuring the world could flourish.<ref name="2024 Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]''</ref>

After discovering the changes pioneered by Karga,<ref name="Chapter 17" /> the pirates of Gorian Shard's pirate crew attempted to reclaim Nevarro as a heaven for crime via a [[Pirate siege on Nevarro|planetary siege]]<ref name="Chapter 21" /> launched with the approval of their allies in Gideon's Imperial remnant.<ref name="Chapter 23">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 23: The Spies}}</ref> However, the return of the Mandalorian Tribe to Nevarro—including Djarin and Grogu—repelled the invasion.<ref name="Chapter 21" /> Active around the same time, the bounty hunter [[Pokkit]] was active but, in her capacity as a Guild hunter, believed she only was afforded "low-rent" work. In time, she managed to find work bounty hunting for a singular private client, opening a new chapter of her career. At some point prior, she had lost a bounty to the pirate [[Jod Na Nawood]], whom she knew as "Dash Zentin" and finally had a chance to reunite with on the leisure planet [[Lanupa]].<ref name="SC5" />

====Distancing from the shattered Empire====
{{Quote|The guild isn't what it used to be, and because of that there could be no better time for the Resistance to forge a partnership.|Vice Admiral Amilyn Holdo, ''The Rebel Files''|<ref name="Rebel Files" />}}
[[File:First_Order_Military.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The First Order's strong ideological beliefs alienated the Guild.]]
By the time of the [[Resistance]], the Bounty Hunters' Guild had reformed into an organization Resistance [[Vice Admiral]] [[Amilyn Holdo]] saw as a potential partner against the [[First Order]], an Imperial remnant with strong ideological beliefs that the fellow Resistance member, [[Caluan Ematt]], speculated to be the reason behind the Order's reluctance to do business with the guild. With reservations, Ematt agreed with Holdo's comment in ''The Rebel Files'' that the Resistance could form a successful partnership with the guild.<ref name="Rebel Files" />

Decades prior, with the Empire's defeat in the [[Battle of Endor]], the Guild hunter [[Seleno Chandro]] eventually left the organization as he gained a reputation for capturing Imperial fugitives. That reputation had left the former Guild hunter paranoid of First Order reprisals. Nonetheless, Chandro<ref name="TROS VD">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> was among the countless individuals who heeded the Resistance's call for assistance over the [[Sith]] planet [[Exegol]] and aided in the destruction of the [[Sith]] Order in the [[Battle of Exegol]], which also ushered in the [[Uprising against the First Order|destruction of the First Order]].<ref name="Episode IX">{{Film|IX}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Bounty Hunters' Guild was first mentioned in the [[2014]] [[canon]] junior novel ''[[Ezra's Gamble]]'', written by [[Ryder Windham]].<ref name="EG" /> It first appeared in [[Chapter 1: The Mandalorian|Chapter 1]] of [[Jon Favreau]]'s [[2019]] television show ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'', directed by [[Dave Filoni]],<ref name="Chapter 1" /> which aired on [[November 12]], 2019.<ref name="DTCI">{{WebCite|url=https://lumiere-a.akamaihd.net/v1/documents/the_mandalorian_project_one-sheet_10_ec1e005f.pdf|text=The Mandalorian Media Kit|work=[https://dtcimedia.disney.com Disney Direct-to-Consumer & International]|archivedate=20230315011507}}</ref> The Guild originated in the [[1998]] [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] novel ''[[The Mandalorian Armor]]'', written by [[K. W. Jeter]].<ref name="Mandalorian Armor">''[[The Mandalorian Armor]]''</ref>
